answered.question: Do the NFL.com terms permit the systematic capture that several requirements ask for?
answered.answer: No, not without express prior written consent. Section 1.3 of the NFL.com Terms of Service, updated 16 May 2024, states: "Systematic retrieval of data or other content from the Services, whether to create or compile, directly or indirectly, a collection, compilation, database, or directory, is prohibited absent our express prior written consent." That blocks automated multi-day snapshots, a scheduled Wednesday-to-kickoff series, a past-season archive and any per-club sweep. It is a permission blocker, not a work blocker: no amount of engineering substitutes for consent.
answered.how: Read from the official NFL legal page on 2026-11-16 at https://www.nfl.com/legal/terms/. Independently read by this session; an earlier session reached the same conclusion and recorded it as DEC-01.

open_data.question: What is the play rate for each game-status designation (Out, Doubtful, Questionable, no designation)?
open_data.would_close_it: Join several seasons of dated designations to the official inactive lists and count how often each designation actually played.
open_data.number_needed: A confidence interval on the play rate for each designation, from at least 2 seasons.
open_data.probe: Archive the official weekly inactives per game for past seasons, then join on player and game. The route is the same official family already read successfully this session.

open_data.question: How deep does a replacement actually go, measured in strings travelled?
open_data.would_close_it: A verified depth order per club, then count the number of strings between the missing player and the player who started.
open_data.number_needed: Strings travelled per replacement, for 32 of 32 clubs.
open_data.probe: Verify one of the two candidate depth routes for all 32 clubs, or obtain an official snap-count source and derive depth from playing time.

open_data.question: Does the Wednesday designation predict the Friday designation?
open_data.would_close_it: Three or more dated captures per week, then measure the transition matrix between them.
open_data.number_needed: Transition counts between designations across the week, for at least one full season.
open_data.probe: Run the capture on a schedule, Wednesday through kickoff. This session established the capture shape but not the schedule.

open_data.question: What is the closing-line value of an originated number?
open_data.would_close_it: An opening price and a closing price for the same market, both captured before kickoff.
open_data.number_needed: Closing-line value per market, measured over a prospective window.
open_data.probe: Obtain a price source that records an opening number. No source obtained so far records one, which is flag OD-02.

open_data.question: What is the licence and provenance of the committed price files?
open_data.would_close_it: A written determination of the terms under which each file may be used.
open_data.number_needed: A licence note recorded against every price file used in a published backtest.
open_data.probe: Read the terms of the originating repository or vendor and record the answer. Until then the files stay quarantined, which is flag OD-01.

open_data.question: What is the venue, roof status and surface of every fixture?
open_data.would_close_it: One game-centre read per fixture, capturing the Game Info block.
open_data.number_needed: Venue, roof and surface for 32 of 32 clubs, confirmed by game-centre read rather than by link parameter.
open_data.probe: This session proved the field exists and read one fixture. Extend the capture to one game per club.

open_data.question: Do the 2026 kickoff and onside-kick rules change totals or fourth-quarter comeback rates?
open_data.would_close_it: The rule text committed before the evaluation window opens, then a measured comparison against that frozen text.
open_data.number_needed: A pre-registered estimate with an interval, published with its registration commit hash.
open_data.probe: Commit the rule text and sample window to git first. Nothing may be measured before that commit exists, or the result is post hoc and must be discarded.

open_data.question: Is any apparent skill larger than the control baselines?
open_data.would_close_it: A random-picks control and a favourites-only control scored on exactly the same events as every candidate.
open_data.number_needed: A lower bound on benchmark-relative skill above zero after a multiplicity adjustment.
open_data.probe: Publish the control rows with every leaderboard run. The controls are defined but have never been scored on real events.

owner_decisions.question: Which of the two implementations of the same eight origination requirements is canonical?
owner_decisions.why_it_blocks: A market board on the main dashboard (session a77d40e1) and the origination desk (session 2c3cef39) implement the same brief on different inputs. Their model lines can differ because the inputs do.
owner_decisions.number_needed: A recorded designation of one canonical implementation, or a decision to merge both onto one input set.
owner_decisions.note: Recorded as flag OD-16 and as question Q-21 on the origination desk. It is the largest loose end on the site.

owner_decisions.question: Should raw row-level data stay in the public repository?
owner_decisions.why_it_blocks: The public site currently carries row-level transcriptions. The requirement asks for a public analysis layer and a private data layer.
owner_decisions.number_needed: A recorded decision, with the terms of use read before anyone acts on it.
owner_decisions.note: Blocked until the terms are read. Do not move data first and read the terms afterwards.

owner_decisions.question: Is a funded reward schedule wanted for the leaderboard competition?
owner_decisions.why_it_blocks: The competition policy and the divisions exist, but no reward is funded and no strategy has qualified.
owner_decisions.number_needed: A published reward schedule, or a recorded decision to run the competition unfunded.
owner_decisions.note: Not urgent: no strategy has cleared the proper-score gate, so there is nothing to reward yet.

owner_decisions.question: Which improvement path should be built first?
owner_decisions.why_it_blocks: Four candidate paths are costed on the suggestions board and none is chosen.
owner_decisions.number_needed: One path marked chosen, with the others left unranked rather than ranked by someone who has not decided.
owner_decisions.note: This is the decision the suggestions board exists to capture. Nothing marked awaiting decision has been implemented.

owner_decisions.question: May this project systematically retrieve NFL.com content, and what happens to the capture already committed?
owner_decisions.why_it_blocks: Ten or more requirement lines ask for scheduled or repeated capture. NFL.com Terms section 1.3 prohibits systematic retrieval without express prior written consent. This session itself made six fetches and committed one verbatim capture, so the question applies to work already in the repository, not only to work not yet started.
owner_decisions.number_needed: A recorded decision with one of three outcomes: seek and obtain written consent, re-scope the affected requirements to what the terms permit, or remove the committed capture. Until one is recorded, no further capture should be run.
owner_decisions.note: Recorded as flag DD-13. An earlier session made the same finding as DEC-01 and deliberately did not build the scraper. This session reached the same conclusion independently after reading the terms page.

owner_decisions.question: Three per-requirement readiness registers now exist. Which one is canonical?
owner_decisions.why_it_blocks: readiness/ publishes 82 requirement rows, verification/ publishes 74, and this desk publishes 73. Three counts for the same brief is worse than two: a reviewer cannot tell which number is the project's.
owner_decisions.number_needed: One register designated canonical, with the other two labelled as superseded or merged.
owner_decisions.note: Extends VF-11, which recorded two. Recorded here as flag DD-14. This session did not read either other register line by line, so it does not claim to know which is better; that is the decision.
